title: Jude and the Orchard
premise: Jude Ashgrove, a lighthouse keeper's grandson and part-time novelist, has spent fifteen years hiding from a scandal that destroyed his family's orchard and his faith in justice. When his sister begs him to bring a date to the Ashgrove family reunion, he hires Wren Calloway, a sharp-tongued archivist who turns out to be investigating the very land deal that ruined them. Their fake romance becomes real just as Jude uncovers proof that his uncle, now a beloved county judge, framed Jude's late father for the orchard's collapse. Choosing justice outside the law, Jude and Wren expose the truth publicly at the harvest festival, costing Jude his inheritance but winning him back the community, the restored orchard, and a love that stays after the last train leaves.
about_author: Ulyana Dunmore is a former small-town newspaper reporter who writes romances about people who learn that home is a decision, not an address. She lives on a coastal peninsula with an opinionated dog and a garden she refuses to weed on principle.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Fifteen years after fleeing Hollow Creek, Jude keeps his life deliberately small: a rented cottage, a half-finished novel, a job cataloging the town library's archives. A letter arrives summoning him to the Ashgrove reunion, and with it, panic. Beat: the safe walls of his life shown cracking at the first knock.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His sister Marisol pleads: come to the reunion, but don't come alone—Uncle Alden will interrogate any unattached Ashgrove for hours. On impulse, Jude answers a notice-board ad offering 'dates for difficult occasions.' He meets Wren Calloway over bad coffee and negotiates terms like a coward signing a treaty. Beat: nervous comedy masking old wounds.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Good Shoes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren takes the gig for the money and because Hollow Creek is her real destination—the county records office there holds deeds tied to a story she's chasing. She studies Jude's file of family grudges and finds a man rehearsing invisibility. Beat: intrigue; Wren sees more in Jude than he intends to show.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Ashgrove estate glitters with cider lanterns and old money. Uncle Alden, now Judge Ashgrove, greets Jude with warm condescension while relatives whisper about his father's 'crime.' Wren plays the devoted girlfriend flawlessly—too flawlessly. Beat: humiliation and unexpected shelter as Wren deflects Alden's cruelty.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Between toasts, Jude and Wren escape to the derelict orchard where he grew up. She asks real questions; he gives real answers for the first time in years. They almost kiss under the last surviving apple tree, then retreat into the fiction they're being paid to perform. Beat: longing recognized and denied.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Secret
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses nothing but works fast: her late mother was an orchard laborer whose wrongful dismissal broke her, and Wren has spent years tracing the fraudulent land transfer that gutted Ashgrove Orchard. The signature on the deed belongs to Alden. Beat: resolve hardening into obsession; guilt about using Jude begins.

chapters.title: Extension Clause
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The reunion ends, but neither cancels the arrangement. Wren claims she needs 'a few more appearances' for credibility; Jude knows he simply doesn't want the last train to take her. They fall into a rhythm of staged dates that stop feeling staged. Beat: quiet joy, both pretending it's temporary.

chapters.title: What Father Buried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Sorting his father's stored belongings in the lighthouse cellar, Jude finds a ledger his father kept secretly—records proving the orchard's finances were drained years before the 'embezzlement' that destroyed him. Jude's hands shake. Beat: grief reignited; suspicion of Alden becomes certainty forming.

chapters.title: Rain on the Records Office
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren pulls the original deed from county archives during a storm and photographs it, but a clerk mentions Judge Ashgrove personally reviewed the file last month. Someone is covering tracks. She comes home soaked to find Jude waiting with tea he pretends is casual. Beat: danger closing in; intimacy deepening without permission.

chapters.title: The Novel He Won't Finish
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads Jude's abandoned manuscript hidden in his desk—a thinly veiled story of a boy watching his father be destroyed by a town that chose comfort over truth. She confronts him gently; he shatters, then lets her stay the night, chaste and terrified. Beat: vulnerability as turning point toward trust.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol discovers the dating arrangement via a crumpled invoice and confronts Wren—not with anger, but with a plea: her father died broken, and if Wren's digging can prove what Marisol always suspected, she'll help. Beat: alliance formed; the fake romance gains a witness who wants it real.

chapters.title: Judge Ashgrove Invites You to Dinner
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alden invites Jude and Wren to dinner, all charm, and mentions—with pointed pleasantness—that he's heard 'an archivist has been asking questions.' The threat is velvet. That night Jude realizes Wren never told him why she came. Betrayal flickers. Beat: menace plus first fracture between them.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jude accuses Wren of using him; Wren accuses Jude of hiding behind safety his whole life. Both are right. She shows him the forged deed evidence; he shows her his father's ledger. The pieces interlock. Beat: rage transmuted into partnership, and an honest kiss in the lighthouse wind.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Ran
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They track down Tomas Reyes, the orchard foreman who testified against Jude's father and then vanished. Found dying in a care home, Tomas confesses Alden paid him to lie—and gives them a signed statement. Beat: hope surging, shadowed by mortality and the weight of fifteen lost years.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A lawyer friend warns them: the statute of limitations is dead, Alden owns the local courts, and going public means lawsuits, ruin, and Alden disowning them both. Jude must choose between the inheritance he's finally being offered and the truth he's finally able to speak. Beat: dark night of the soul; the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Devil in Corduroy
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Alden offers Jude everything: the estate, the orchard, the family name restored—if he hands over the documents and sends the archivist away. For one long evening, Jude is tempted by the belonging he's starved for. Beat: corruption's seduction rendered intimate; Jude walks out into the rain empty-handed and free.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tomorrow's festival is Alden's crowning public moment—he'll announce the orchard restoration as his legacy project. The team plans to interrupt it: Marisol has copies, Tomas's statement is notarized, and the regional paper's editor owes Wren a favor. Beat: tension coiling tight; love confessed quietly the night before everything might burn.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Deed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the festival, before three hundred townspeople, Alden takes the stage. Jude interrupts, reads the forged deed aloud, and Marisol distributes copies. Chaos, denial, then Tomas's recorded voice plays over the loudspeakers. Beat: climax—truth spoken outside any courtroom, the crowd as jury.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Apples
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alden resigns under investigation; some neighbors thank Jude, others spit at his feet. The estate is frozen, the inheritance poisoned. Jude feels lighter than he's ever been standing in the stripped-bare orchard, wondering what grows next. Beat: cost acknowledged, freedom tasted, grief finally given room.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Months later, the community replants the orchard together—laborers' descendants, Marisol, even hesitant old families. Wren's exposé wins an award she doesn't attend because she's elbow-deep in soil. She and Jude have stopped calling anything fake. Beat: belonging rebuilt collectively; love rooted in shared work.

chapters.title: The Finished Manuscript
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude finishes his novel and dedicates it to 'the ones who stayed.' An editor calls with an offer; Alden's trial looms but no longer defines him. He asks Wren, formally and trembling, to stay—not hired, not arranged, chosen. Beat: full-circle resolution of the opening's fear.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Autumn again, one year on. The new trees bear their first small fruit. At the station platform where Wren once bought a one-way ticket, she tears it up instead. They walk home through the orchard as the last train passes without either of them on it. Beat: peace earned; the ending mirrors and answers the beginning.
